data.description:
# Major-explosion cue and constants

## Goal
Add an exported `playMajorExplosionSound()` to `src/audio/effects.ts`: a new dedicated, layered "major explosion" cue (impact thump + descending body + filtered-noise tail), distinct from the generic `playDestructionSound()` and the player `playPlayerDestructionSound()`, with every tuning value exposed as an exported `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_*` constant, plus unit tests.

## User story
As a player, when the level timer hits zero and my remaining enemies detonate, I hear a large, heavy explosion cue so the moment reads as a major event rather than a silent animation.

## Scope
- New exported `playMajorExplosionSound()` in `src/audio/effects.ts`, mirroring the layered structure of `playPlayerDestructionSound()`: (1) deep impact thump, (2) descending body sweep, (3) filtered-noise shrapnel tail.
- Every frequency endpoint, duration, layer gain and the voice cap exposed as exported `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_*` constants (no inline tuning literals in the cue body).
- All layers route through the existing master SFX gain (`ensureMasterGain`) so SFX volume/mute plumbing applies.
- Unit tests in `src/audio/effects.test.ts`; master routing tests in `src/audio/effectsMaster.test.ts`.
- The voice limiter itself is a separate child (`Major-explosion voice limiter`); this item may export the `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_MAX_VOICES` constant but wires no limiter logic.

## Constraints
- Procedural Web Audio synthesis only; zero external audio assets (GDD §7.3).
- Must never throw when audio is unavailable (mirror the existing safe no-op pattern).
- Must not modify `playDestructionSound()` or `playPlayerDestructionSound()` behaviour.
- Keep layer gains within the documented cue ceiling so the cue does not drown other SFX.

## Key Files
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — new cue + `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_*` constants.
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — unit tests.
- `src/audio/effectsMaster.test.ts` — master volume/mute routing tests.

## References
- Parent: AH-0MUJ1YZJ9008O4RC (AC1, AC5); GDD §7.3 Audio Direction.
- Precedent: `playPlayerDestructionSound()` (AH-0MUDY2ID7006VY3A).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` `blip()` / `ensureMasterGain()` helpers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `playMajorExplosionSound()` is exported from `src/audio/effects.ts` and is a safe no-op that never throws without an `AudioContext`.
- The cue is layered with at least three distinct audio nodes: a deep impact thump, a descending body sweep and a filtered-noise tail.
- Every frequency endpoint, duration and layer gain is an exported `MAJOR_EXPLOSION_*` constant (no inline tuning literals in the cue body).
- All cue layers route through the existing master SFX gain so SFX volume/mute apply.
- Unit tests assert layer count, constant-driven amplitude/duration, master routing, the no-AudioContext no-op, and that the cue differs from `playDestructionSound()` and `playPlayerDestructionSound()`.
- `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` pass.
- Covers parent AC1 and AC5.
